chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The wine drinker is not visited when he is sick, nor is his funeral attended, nor is his testimony verified when he testifies, nor is he given in marriage when he proposes, nor is he entrusted with a trust.'

key_terms.شَارِبُ الْخَمْرِ: The wine drinker (habitual consumer of khamr)

ai.seo_question: What are the five social and legal penalties for a wine drinker according to this hadith from al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the social stigma and legal disqualification of the habitual wine drinker (sharib al-khamr), reflecting the Shia juristic view that intoxication corrupts one's moral integrity and trustworthiness. It highlights five specific deprivations: lack of visitation during illness, exclusion from funeral prayers, invalidation of testimony, difficulty in marriage proposals, and unreliability in trusts. This ruling underscores the connection between ritual purity and social reliability in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from IBn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The wine drinker should neither be consoled when he is sick, nor should his funeral be attended, nor should he be verified when he testifies, nor should he be given in marriage when he proposes, nor should he be relied upon an entrustment’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘

The wine drinker must not be visited when he is sick. His funeral must not be attended, he must not be relied on when he testifies and must not be married when he proposes for marriage. You must not trust him about a trust.’”
